english.title: Forge / alter / use / lend a PSV operator's licence / certificate / disc / document with intent to deceive
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to deceive,

(A)_[forged]_
(B)_[altered]_
(C)_[used]_
(D)_[lent to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)]_
(E)_[allowed to be used by **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)]_

(F)_[a licence under Part II of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(G)_[a certificate of initial fitness under section 6 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(H)_[a certificate under section 10 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981 that a vehicle conformed to a type vehicle]_
(I)_[an operator's disc under section 18 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981]_
(J)_[a certificate under section 21 of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981 as to the repute, financial standing or professional competence of a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)]_
(K)_[a control document issued in pursuance of regulation 4 of the Road Transport (International Passenger Services) Regulations 2018]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 65(2)(a) of the Public Passenger Vehicles Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
with intent to deceive
forged / altered / used / lent / allowed to be used
a part II licence / certificate of initial fitness / section 10 certificate / operators disc / section 21 certificate / control document

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) This offence applies from the 1st April 2025 due to changes by SI 2024/1370 Road Transport (International Passenger Services) (Amendment) Regulations 2024. For the offence before this date, see H16533.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: A fine
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
